title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return its **maximum depth**.

A binary tree's maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node. An empty tree has a maximum depth of `0`, and a tree with a single root node has a maximum depth of `1`.
hints: The maximum depth of an empty tree is 0.
For any non-empty node, its maximum depth is `1 + max(maxDepth(node.left), maxDepth(node.right))`.
You can also count levels iteratively with Breadth-First Search (BFS) using a queue.

examples.explanation: The longest root-to-leaf paths are 3 -> 20 -> 15 and 3 -> 20 -> 7, each containing 3 nodes.
The only root-to-leaf path is 1 -> 2, which has 2 nodes.
